q.s: Which of the following Early Harappan sites anticipates Mature Harappan buildings and pottery?
q.x: Kot Diji (like Kalibangan) shows pre-urban forms that anticipate the Mature Harappan phase, pointing to gradual, local urbanisation; the others are Neolithic/Chalcolithic sites outside the Harappan zone.

q.s: Harappan cities were laid out on which pattern?
o: Grid pattern with streets crossing at right angles
Irregular pattern along a river bank
Radial pattern around a central temple
q.x: Harappan streets ran north-south and east-west, crossing at right angles, with house doors opening on side lanes.

q.s: Which animal is the most common motif on Harappan seals?
q.x: The one-horned 'unicorn' is the commonest seal motif; the humped bull is also frequent.

q.s: Which of the following animals is NOT depicted on Harappan seals?
q.x: The cow is not shown on Harappan seals, while the rhinoceros, humped bull and tiger are.

q.s: Which of the following is cited in support of the view that the Harappans were ruled by priests?
q.x: The citadels, the Great Bath and the steatite 'Priest-King' bust are cited for priestly rule, though the evidence is not conclusive.

q.s: Which of the following was a feature of the Late Harappan phase?
q.x: The Late Harappan phase was chalcolithic with regionally varied pottery; the uniformity of seals, bricks and weights and long-distance trade were lost.

q.s: Coins of which Shaka ruler were re-struck by Gautamiputra Satakarni?
q.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated the Kshaharata Nahapana and re-struck his coins (Jogalthembi hoard).

q.s: Which inscription hails Gautamiputra Satakarni as the destroyer of the Shakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas?
q.x: The Nasik Prashasti of his mother Gautami Balashri records this title.

q.s: In the Rig Veda, the Panis are described as:
q.x: The Panis were non-Aryan cattle-holders and traders condemned for their greed.

q.s: In the later Vedic period, the teacher who taught the Veda for a livelihood was called:
q.x: The Upadhyaya taught for a livelihood, while the Acharya taught the Veda without charging a fee.

q.s: Initiation into Vedic study was marked by which samskara?
q.x: Upanayana initiated Vedic study; Chudakarma was only the tonsure of the child.

q.s: The Mahavamsa, the Sri Lankan Buddhist chronicle, was written in:
q.x: The Mahavamsa of Mahanama is in Pali; the Dohakosa is in Apabhramsa and the Divyavadana in Sanskrit.

q.s: The four gateways (toranas) of the Sanchi stupa were added under the:
q.x: The toranas are Satavahana additions; the Shungas gave the stone casing and railings.

q.s: The Sanchi stupa is located in which district of Madhya Pradesh?
q.x: Sanchi lies in Raisen district; it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989.

q.s: The atomic theory of the Ajivikas influenced which later school of philosophy?
q.x: The Vaisheshika is the atomist school of Indian philosophy, influenced by Ajivika ideas.

q.s: Who among the following was the leader of the Ajivika sect?
q.x: Makkhali Gosala led the Ajivikas; Ajita Kesakambalin was a materialist teacher.

q.s: Ramatirtham, an important Jain hill centre of Andhra, is in which district?
q.x: Ramatirtham in Vizianagaram district was a Jain (and Buddhist) hill centre.

q.s: The medical work Kalyanakaraka was written at Ramatirtham by:
q.x: Ugradityacharya, a Jain teacher, wrote the Kalyanakaraka at Ramatirtham.

q.s: In Kautilya's Saptanga theory of the state, which element comes last?
q.x: The order is Swami, Amatya, Janapada, Durga, Kosha, Danda and Mitra.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven elements of Kautilya's Saptanga theory?
q.x: Shatru (enemy) is not one of the seven elements.

q.s: Which Ashokan edict, discovered in 1915, first proved that 'Piyadasi' was Ashoka?
q.x: The Maski minor rock edict in Raichur district names 'Ashoka', confirming the identity.

q.s: Kanaganahalli, where a stone portrait of Ashoka labelled 'Ranyo Asoko' was found, is on the banks of which river?
q.x: Kanaganahalli near Sannati (Karnataka) is on the Bhima.

q.s: Who among the following was the author of the Sanskrit drama Ratnavali?
q.x: Harshavardhana wrote Ratnavali, Priyadarshika and Nagananda; Banabhatta was his court poet.

q.s: Grahavarman, husband of Harsha's sister Rajyashri, belonged to which dynasty?
q.x: Grahavarman was the Maukhari king of Kannauj.

q.s: Who ruled at Thanesar immediately before Harshavardhana?
q.x: Harsha's elder brother Rajyavardhana succeeded their father Prabhakaravardhana and was killed by Shashanka.

q.s: The first round of the Chalukya-Pallava conflict was fought between Pulakesin II and:
q.x: Pulakesin II fought Mahendravarman I first; Narasimhavarman I defeated him in the second round and took Vatapi.

q.s: Madhura Vijayam, which describes the conquest of the Madurai Sultanate, was written by:
q.x: Gangadevi, wife of Kumara Kampana, wrote Madhura Vijayam.

q.s: Which Telugu Brahmin convert became the wazir of Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
q.x: Malik Maqbul (Khan-i-Jahan), originally Jagannatha Pandit, became Firoz Shah's wazir.

q.s: After its capture by the Tughlaqs in 1323, Warangal was renamed:
q.x: Warangal became Sultanpur; Daulatabad was the renamed Devagiri.

q.s: Ghazi Malik (Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq) was Governor of Dipalpur (Punjab) under:
q.x: He was Alauddin Khalji's governor of Dipalpur before founding the Tughlaq dynasty.

q.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, an iqta was:
o: An assignment of revenue in lieu of salary
A military rank based on horses
q.x: The iqta was a transferable revenue assignment, not ownership; muqtis were rotated every few years until Firoz Tughlaq.

q.s: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud, was written by:
q.x: Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote it; Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir under Aibak.

q.s: Isami's Futuh-us-Salatin was written at the court of the:
q.x: Isami wrote it at the Bahmani court around 1350.

q.s: The king 'Chandra' of the Mehrauli Iron Pillar is identified with:
q.x: The Iron Pillar is attributed to Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT part of the 'Qutb Minar and its Monuments' World Heritage Site?
q.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's tomb is at Tughlaqabad; the others are in the Qutb complex (WHS 1993).

q.s: Amir Khusrau's Tughluqnama deals with:
o: Meeting of Bughra Khan and Kaiqubad
q.x: Tughluqnama is on Ghiyasuddin's rise; Nuh Sipihr praises India under Mubarak Shah.

q.s: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, called Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani, belonged to which Sufi order?
q.x: Sirhindi was a Naqshbandi and criticised Akbar's religious ideas from an orthodox standpoint.

q.s: Who wrote the Dabistan-i-Mazahib, which called Din-i-Ilahi a religion?
q.x: Mohsin Fani wrote Dabistan-i-Mazahib.

q.s: The du-aspa sih-aspa rank in the mansabdari system was introduced by:
q.x: Jahangir introduced it, first for Mahabat Khan; Akbar introduced the mansabdari system itself.

q.s: Who among the following built the Lohagarh fort at Bharatpur?
q.x: Suraj Mal, called the 'Plato of the Jat tribe', built Lohagarh.

q.s: The Jantar Mantar observatories at Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Varanasi and Mathura were built by:
q.x: Sawai Jai Singh II of Amber built all five observatories.

q.s: Which Mughal painter was sent by Jahangir to Persia to paint Shah Abbas and his court?
q.x: Bishan Das went with Jahangir's embassy to Persia.

q.s: Daswant, the son of a potter, was a leading painter at the court of:
q.x: Daswant and Basawan were leading masters of Akbar's atelier.

q.s: Among the disciples of Ramananda, Raidas was by profession a:
q.x: Raidas was a cobbler; Kabir was a weaver, Sena a barber and Dhanna a Jat.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a disciple of Ramananda?
q.x: Kabir, Raidas, Pipa, Sena and Dhanna were Ramananda's disciples; Guru Nanak was not.

q.s: The Tallapaka family of composers is associated with which shrine?
q.x: Annamacharya and the Tallapaka family sang at Tirumala.

q.s: Bhakta Ramadasu (Kancherla Gopanna) is associated with which temple?
q.x: Ramadasu built the Rama temple at Bhadrachalam; Kshetrayya is linked with Muvva.

q.s: In which year did Shivaji die?
q.x: Shivaji died in 1680; 1689 is the year Sambhaji was executed and 1674 that of his coronation.

q.s: Madanna and Akkanna were ministers of which kingdom?
q.x: They served Abul Hasan Tana Shah of Golconda and arranged his 1677 alliance with Shivaji.

q.s: Which of the following European trading companies was formed earliest?
q.x: English 1600, Dutch 1602, Danish 1616, French 1664.

q.s: The French East India Company was formed in 1664 on the initiative of:
q.x: Colbert, minister of Louis XIV, set up the company in 1664.

q.s: Tranquebar on the Coromandel coast was a settlement of the:
q.x: Tranquebar was Danish; Serampore was their Bengal base.

q.s: Chinsura in Bengal was a settlement of the:
q.x: Chinsura was Dutch, Chandernagore French and Banquibazar the Ostend Company's.

q.s: Who led the Revolt of 1857 at Lucknow?
q.x: Begum Hazrat Mahal led at Lucknow; Nana Sahib at Kanpur and Kunwar Singh at Jagdishpur.

q.s: Who was the real military leader of the rebels at Delhi in 1857?
q.x: General Bakht Khan, who came from Bareilly, led the rebel forces at Delhi.

q.s: Khan Bahadur Khan led the Revolt of 1857 at:
q.x: Khan Bahadur Khan proclaimed himself Nawab Nizam at Bareilly in Rohilkhand.

q.s: The name 'Rayalaseema' was proposed in 1928 by:
q.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao proposed it; the Nandyal Andhra Mahasabha approved it.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the districts ceded by the Nizam in 1800?
q.x: On 12 October 1800 the Nizam ceded Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary in lieu of the subsidy.

q.s: The 'Sunset Law' is associated with which land revenue system?
q.x: Under the Permanent Settlement an estate was sold if revenue was unpaid by sunset of the due date.

q.s: Which Act gave occupancy rights to tenants in Bengal and Bihar?
q.x: The Bengal Tenancy Act 1885; the Haftam and Panjam Regulations instead strengthened zamindars.

q.s: The Montagu Declaration promising progressive realisation of responsible government was made in:
q.x: It was made on 20 August 1917; the Montagu-Chelmsford Report followed in 1918.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Montagu Declaration is correct?
o: It was made in response to pressure from the Swaraj Party.
It promised immediate Dominion Status to India.
It was issued after the Government of India Act 1919.
Lord Chelmsford was the Viceroy when it was made.
q.x: Chelmsford was Viceroy and Montagu Secretary of State; the pressure came from the Home Rule movement (the Swaraj Party arose only in 1923).

q.s: Which Brahmo leader of Andhra joined the Justice Party, leading to splits in the movement?
q.x: Splits after Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu joined the Justice Party contributed to the Brahmo decline in Andhra.

q.s: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856 was passed under which Governor-General?
q.x: It was passed under Canning in 1856; Dalhousie had left earlier that year.

q.s: Under whose leadership was the first widow remarriage held in Bengal in December 1856?
q.x: Vidyasagar organised the first remarriage on 7 December 1856.

q.s: The Theosophical Society was founded in 1875 at:
q.x: Blavatsky and Olcott founded it at New York in 1875; it came to India in 1879.

q.s: Who among the following were the founders of the Theosophical Society?
q.x: Blavatsky and Olcott were the founders; Annie Besant joined later.

q.s: Rast Goftar, the organ of the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha, was edited by:
q.x: Dadabhai Naoroji edited Rast Goftar; the Sabha worked for girls' education and Parsi marriage reform.

q.s: The Butler Committee (1927) was appointed to examine:
o: Reform of the Indian Civil Service
Relations between princely states and the Paramount Power
q.x: Chaired by Harcourt Butler, it examined relations between the princely states and the Paramount Power.

q.s: The Purna Swaraj resolution was adopted at which Congress session?
q.x: At Lahore in 1929, after the one-year deadline set at Calcutta in 1928 lapsed.

q.s: Who presided over the Lahore session of the Congress (1929)?
q.x: Jawaharlal Nehru presided; Motilal Nehru presided at Calcutta in 1928.

q.s: Who led the defence of the INA officers in the Red Fort trials?
q.x: Bhulabhai Desai led the INA Defence Committee's counsel.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the INA defence team at the Red Fort?
q.x: Nehru, Asaf Ali, Katju, Sapru and Sarat Bose were in the defence; Patel was not.

q.s: Who led the Chirala-Perala movement against the formation of a municipality?
q.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya led the residents' exodus from Chirala to Ramnagar.

q.s: The JVP Committee on linguistic states consisted of Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and:
q.x: Its 1949 report first rejected linguistic states, putting unity and security first.

q.s: Who is called the 'Iron Man of India' for integrating the princely states?
q.x: Patel integrated over 560 princely states into the Union, with V.P. Menon as his secretary.

q.s: The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was led by:
q.x: The women of Bardoli gave Patel the title 'Sardar' after this no-tax campaign.

q.s: On Justice Mishra's report, Bellary taluk was given to:
q.x: Bellary taluk went to Mysore, while Rayadurg, Adoni and Alur went to Andhra.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the common High Court of the two states was located at:
q.x: Section 30 of the Act provided for a common High Court at Hyderabad.

q.s: Who became Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh when President's Rule ended in December 1973?
q.x: Jalagam Vengala Rao took office after the State's first President's Rule (January-December 1973).

q.s: The Jai Andhra agitation was called off in October 1973 after the announcement of the:
q.x: It ended after the Six-Point Formula; the 32nd Amendment followed in December 1973.

q.s: Who among the following was a leader of the Jai Andhra movement of 1972-73?
q.x: Kakani Venkataratnam, B.V. Subba Reddy and Tenneti Viswanatham led Jai Andhra; the others are linked with the Telangana movements.

q.s: The K.C. Sivaramakrishnan Committee (2014) was set up to:
o: Recommend new districts for Andhra Pradesh
Divide the assets of the composite State
Suggest options for the new capital of Andhra Pradesh
q.x: The expert committee on the AP capital reported in August 2014 and opposed a single 'super capital'.

q.s: Which was the first North-Eastern State to be carved out of Assam with full statehood?
q.x: Nagaland became a State in 1963.

q.s: Which of the following became a State in 1987?
q.x: Goa, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh became States in 1987; Sikkim in 1975, Meghalaya in 1972 and Nagaland in 1963.

q.s: The Kalamalla inscription, regarded as the first Telugu inscription, was issued by:
q.x: Dhananjaya Varma issued the Kalamalla (Kadapa) inscription; the Pedavegi plates are of the Salankayana Nandivarma II.

q.s: Bavari, who sent sixteen disciples to the Buddha, had settled on the banks of the:
q.x: The Suttanipata says Bavari of Kosala settled on the Godavari in the Assaka region.

q.s: The capital of the Mulaka janapada, neighbour of Assaka, was:
q.x: Mulaka had its capital at Pratishthana (Paithan); Potana was Assaka's capital.

q.s: Many relics of the Amaravati stupa are today in the British Museum, London and the Government Museum at:
q.x: Amaravati sculptures were taken to London and Madras (Chennai) museums.

q.s: International Museum Day is observed every year on:
q.x: 18 May is International Museum Day; 18 April is World Heritage Day.

q.s: Which ruler assumed the title 'Dakshinapatheshwara' (Lord of the Deccan)?
q.x: Pulakesin II; Harsha was called Sakalottarapathanatha.

q.s: Which of the following ruler-title pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Samudragupta was Kaviraja; Dakshinapatheshwara was Pulakesin II's title.

q.s: The Pallava king who destroyed Vatapi in 642 CE and took the title 'Vatapikonda' was:
q.x: Narasimhavarman I defeated and killed Pulakesin II.

q.s: The first capital of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi was:
q.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana ruled from Pishtapura (Pithapuram); Rajahmundry became capital much later.

q.s: Vikramankadevacharita, a biography of Vikramaditya VI, was written by:
q.x: Bilhana, court poet of the Kalyani Chalukya Vikramaditya VI, wrote it.

q.s: In Kakatiya villages, the twelve village servants were known as:
q.x: The Ayagars were paid by a share of produce and rent-free land.

q.s: In the Kakatiya village administration, the Karanam was the:
q.x: The Karanam kept accounts; the Talari was the watchman.

q.s: Which scholar described the Kakatiya age as the 'Golden Age of the Shudras'?
q.x: Talbot used the phrase; Burton Stein proposed the 'segmentary state' model.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the successor states that arose in Andhra after the fall of the Kakatiyas in 1323?
q.x: The Reddis, Musunuris and Recherla Velamas emerged after 1323; the Eastern Gangas were an older Kalinga dynasty.

q.s: The founder of the Reddi kingdom, who expelled the Tughlaq forces and ruled from Addanki, was:
q.x: Prolaya Vema Reddi founded the kingdom with Addanki as capital.

q.s: Which Reddi ruler abolished the tax on gold and developed the port of Motupalli?
q.x: Anavota Reddi developed Motupalli; Racha Vema was the last Kondavidu king.

q.s: Who succeeded Anavema Reddi on the Kondavidu throne?
q.x: Kumaragiri succeeded Anavema; his brother-in-law Kataya Vema later held Rajahmundry and reached Cuttack.

q.s: Akbar annexed Bengal in the year:
q.x: Bengal was annexed in 1576; Gujarat in 1572-73.

q.s: Jaunpur was conquered from the Sharqis by:
q.x: Bahlul Lodi took Jaunpur around 1479.

q.s: Who presented the Kohinoor diamond to Shah Jahan?
q.x: Mir Jumla, the Golconda noble who joined the Mughals, presented it; Tavernier only recorded it.

q.s: The Kohinoor diamond is believed to have come from which mine of the Golconda kingdom?
q.x: Kollur on the Krishna (Guntur district) was the famous Golconda diamond mine.

q.s: The Qutb Shahi kingdom of Golconda was annexed by Aurangzeb in:
q.x: Golconda fell in 1687, a year after Bijapur (1686).

q.s: The Qutb Shahi dynasty of Golconda was founded by:
q.x: Sultan Quli founded it; Malik Ahmad founded the Nizam Shahis of Ahmadnagar.

q.s: Which foreign visitor gave an eyewitness description of Krishnadevaraya's appearance and the 'House of Victory'?
q.x: Domingo Paes described the king and the Mahanavami Dibba.

q.s: Fernao Nuniz visited Vijayanagara during the reign of:
q.x: Nuniz wrote on Krishnadevaraya's rise but visited under Achyutaraya.

q.s: The Recherla Velamas ruled from:
q.x: The Recherla Velamas held Rachakonda and Devarakonda.

q.s: The Ravu family of Velamas is associated with which estate?
q.x: The Ravus held Bobbili; the Velugotis held Venkatagiri.

q.s: Which of the following is characteristic of Vijayanagara temple architecture?
q.x: Vijayanagara temples added kalyana mandapas, tall raya gopurams and pillared corridors.

q.s: In 1953, which town was chosen as the capital of Andhra State?
q.x: Kurnool became the capital, though the PSP wanted Tirupati.

q.s: The Praja Socialist Party (1952) was formed by merging the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party with the:
q.x: The KMPP and the Socialist Party merged to form the PSP in September 1952.

q.s: In 1911, a series of articles in The Hindu on the backward position of the Telugu people was written by:
q.x: Gurunatham of Guntur wrote six articles in April 1911, giving the low share of Andhras in services.

q.s: Andhra Patrika was founded by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao in the year:
q.x: It began as a weekly in 1908; he also started the literary monthly Bharati in 1924.

q.s: Krishna Patrika was founded in 1902 at:
q.x: Konda Venkatappayya and Dasu Narayana Rao founded it at Machilipatnam.

q.s: Who edited Krishna Patrika from 1907 until his death in 1945?
q.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited it for nearly four decades.

q.s: Adibhatla Narayana Dasu is associated with which art form?
q.x: He is the father of Telugu Harikatha, a solo narrative form.

q.s: The Madiga Reservation Porata Samithi (MRPS) was founded in 1994 by:
q.x: Manda Krishna Madiga founded the MRPS on 7 July 1994; he received the Padma Shri in 2025.

q.s: The MRPS was founded at Eedumudi village in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Eedumudi is in Prakasam district.

q.s: The Nandi Awards for films, television and drama are given by the:
q.x: They are a State honour instituted by Andhra Pradesh in 1964; the National Film Awards are presented by the President.

q.s: Which ruler issued coins bearing the image of the Buddha?
q.x: Kanishka's coins depict the Buddha.

q.s: Muhammad Ghori issued some coins bearing the figure of:
q.x: Ghori's coins carried Lakshmi, some with the Arabic Kalma.

q.s: The Age of Consent Act, 1891 was largely the result of the efforts of:
q.x: Behramji Malabari campaigned for raising the age of consent.

q.s: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, a child marriage is:
o: Void from the beginning in all cases
Voidable at the option of the child
q.x: A child marriage under the PCMA 2006 is voidable at the option of the contracting child.

q.s: 'Caste and Race in India' (1932) was written by:
q.x: Ghurye wrote it; Risley is credited with the first 'scientific' definition of caste.

q.s: 'Caste, Class and Power' (1965) is a study by:
q.x: Beteille's study of Sripuram; Dipankar Gupta wrote 'Interrogating Caste' (2000).

q.s: Which of the following is regarded as the main driver of urbanisation?
q.x: Factories draw workers from villages to towns, creating urban centres.

q.s: The Bodo Peace Accord of 2020 created the:
q.x: The 2020 accord created the BTR; the 2003 accord had created the BTC.

q.s: The demand for 'Greater Nagalim' is raised by the:
q.x: The National Socialist Council of Nagaland (NSCN) demands Greater Nagalim.

q.s: The Ambedkar Overseas Vidya Nidhi of Andhra Pradesh provides:
o: Financial help to SC/ST students for higher studies abroad
q.x: It funds overseas higher studies; inter-caste marriages are covered by a separate Dr Ambedkar scheme.

q.s: Article 275(1) of the Constitution provides for:
o: Appointment of a National Commission for STs
Reservation of seats for STs in Lok Sabha
Grants-in-aid for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes
q.x: Central grants under 275(1) are the main economic safeguard for STs and Scheduled Areas.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?
q.x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability; Article 46 directs promotion of SC/ST interests.

q.s: Andhra State, formed on 1 October 1953, was carved out of:
q.x: Andhra State was separated from Madras State after Potti Sriramulu's fast.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Andhra State is correct?
o: It was formed after the SRC report of 1955.
It was formed on 1 October 1953 with Kurnool as capital.
It was carved out of Hyderabad State.
q.x: Andhra State came on 1 October 1953 from Madras State with Kurnool as capital, before the SRC.

q.s: Under the three-capitals plan of Andhra Pradesh, Visakhapatnam was proposed as the:
q.x: Visakhapatnam was proposed as executive, Amaravati legislative and Kurnool judicial capital.

q.s: The AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020 was withdrawn in:
q.x: Both 2020 Acts were withdrawn in November 2021.

q.s: The 'Disha' app of the Andhra Pradesh Police is meant for:
o: Sending SOS alerts with location to the police
Booking free bus travel for women
q.x: Disha is a women's safety app that shares the user's location with police.

q.s: As per NFHS-5, about what share of women were married before 18 years of age?
q.x: NFHS-5 puts it at about 23.3%; 32% of ever-married women faced spousal violence.

q.s: In August 2026 the Union Government opposed applying which concept to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
q.x: The Union argued that income alone does not end caste-based exclusion.

q.s: The Talliki Vandanam scheme of Andhra Pradesh provides:
o: Rs 15,000 a year to mothers of school pupils
Rs 18,750 a year to women aged 45-60
Free APSRTC bus travel for women
q.x: Talliki Vandanam (restructured Amma Vodi) gives Rs 15,000 a year.

q.s: The Stree Shakti scheme of Andhra Pradesh (August 2025) provides:
o: Free APSRTC bus travel for women
q.x: Stree Shakti started on 15 August 2025 with free bus travel for women.

q.s: 'Navaratnalu' (2019-24) was the welfare package of which party's government in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Navaratnalu was the YSRCP government's set of nine flagship promises.

q.s: The African Union became a permanent member of the G20 in 2023 under the presidency of:
q.x: It joined at the New Delhi Summit under India's presidency.

q.s: Where was the first overseas campus of an IIT set up in 2023?
q.x: IIT Madras Zanzibar in Tanzania was the first overseas IIT.

q.s: India established full diplomatic relations with Israel in:
q.x: Under P.V. Narasimha Rao in 1992; Modi became the first Indian PM to visit Israel in 2017.

q.s: Who was the first Indian Prime Minister to visit Israel?
q.x: Narendra Modi visited Israel in 2017.

q.s: The South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement was signed at which SAARC Summit?
q.x: SAFTA was signed at Islamabad in 2004.

q.s: The last SAARC Summit held so far took place at:
q.x: The 18th Summit at Kathmandu was the last; the 2016 Islamabad summit was cancelled after the Uri attack.

q.s: Which country was invited to join BRICS in August 2023 but declined in December 2023?
q.x: Argentina declined; Iran, Egypt and Ethiopia joined.

q.s: Amendment of the federal provisions of the Constitution requires a special majority of Parliament and ratification by:
q.x: Article 368(2) requires ratification by half of the States.

q.s: Admission or establishment of new States can be done by Parliament by:
o: A special majority with State ratification
q.x: Under Articles 2 and 4 such laws are passed by simple majority and are not amendments under Article 368.

q.s: In direct democracy, 'Recall' means:
o: People's verdict on a political question
Removal of an elected representative before the end of his term
q.x: Recall removes a representative; Initiative proposes, Referendum votes on a law.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment removed the 'split' exception from the Tenth Schedule?
q.x: The 91st Amendment (2003) deleted the one-third split; the 52nd (1985) added the Schedule.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold the Speaker's decision on disqualification under the Tenth Schedule subject to judicial review?
q.x: Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992).

q.s: The theory of 'animism' as the origin of religion is associated with:
q.x: Tylor linked religion's origin to belief in spirits; Frazer proposed magic-religion-science.

q.s: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act was enacted in:
q.x: POCSO 2012; the Child Labour Act is of 1986 and the CPCR Act of 2005.

q.s: 'Sovereignty and integrity of India' was added as a ground for restricting freedoms under Article 19 by the:
q.x: The 16th Amendment added it; 'public order' was added by the 1st Amendment.

q.s: 'Public order' was added as a ground of reasonable restriction in Article 19(2) by the:
q.x: The First Amendment (1951) added public order, friendly relations with foreign States and incitement to an offence.

q.s: The doctrine of 'absolute liability' was laid down by the Supreme Court in the:
q.x: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum gas, 1987) laid down absolute liability.

q.s: The 'public trust doctrine' was applied by the Supreme Court in:
q.x: Kamal Nath (1997); Vellore Citizens adopted the precautionary and polluter-pays principles; Bhikaji Narain gave the doctrine of eclipse.

q.s: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act provided for:
q.x: The 103rd Amendment (124th Bill) gave EWS reservation.

q.s: Constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes was given by the:
q.x: The 102nd Amendment (123rd Bill) inserted Article 338B.

q.s: The order for 27% reservation for OBCs in Central Government posts was issued in August 1990 by the government of:
q.x: V.P. Singh's order took effect from 1993 after Indra Sawhney upheld it.

q.s: Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India (2008) upheld 27% OBC reservation in:
q.x: It upheld the CEI Act, 2006, applying the creamy-layer exclusion to OBCs only.

q.s: Article 350A of the Constitution deals with:
o: Claims of SCs and STs to services
Instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage
q.x: 350A - mother-tongue instruction at primary stage; 350B - Special Officer; 351 - Hindi; 335 - services.

q.s: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is provided for under Article:
q.x: Article 350B provides for the Special Officer, appointed by the President.

q.s: To which of the following Bills must the President give assent, without the option to withhold or return it?
q.x: After the 24th Amendment the President must assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill; a Money Bill can be withheld but not returned.

q.s: 'Consequential seniority' in promotions for SCs and STs was provided by the:
q.x: The 85th Amendment (2001) gave consequential seniority; the 81st kept carry-forward vacancies outside the 50% ceiling.

q.s: The 77th, 81st, 82nd and 85th Amendments on reservation were upheld by the Supreme Court in:
q.x: M. Nagaraj upheld them, subject to conditions.

q.s: Part XIV-A dealing with tribunals was added to the Constitution by the:
q.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Articles 323A and 323B.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT done by the 42nd Amendment, 1976?
o: Transferred forests to the Concurrent List
Restored the term of the Lok Sabha to five years
q.x: The 42nd Amendment raised the term to six years; the 44th restored five years.

q.s: Article 31C protects laws giving effect to which Directive Principles?
q.x: 31C shields laws implementing 39(b) and (c) from challenge under Articles 14 and 19.

q.s: The lower House of Russia's Federal Assembly is the:
q.x: The State Duma is the lower House; the Federation Council the upper.

q.s: Bicameralism at the Centre in India was first introduced by the:
q.x: The 1919 Act made the central legislature bicameral; dyarchy was only in the provinces.

q.s: To be recognised as Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, a party must have at least what share of the House?
q.x: The leader of the largest opposition party with at least one-tenth of the strength is recognised.

q.s: The admissibility of questions, motions and resolutions in the Lok Sabha is decided by the:
q.x: The Speaker decides; his Tenth Schedule decisions are subject to judicial review.

q.s: The Lok Sabha Secretariat functions under the:
q.x: Under Article 98 each House has its own secretariat, independent of the executive.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is correct?
o: The Speaker vacates office as soon as the Lok Sabha is dissolved.
The Deputy Speaker continues in office after dissolution.
The Speaker continues in office after dissolution until the new House first meets.
The Speaker is elected by both Houses of Parliament.
q.x: Under Article 94 the Speaker stays until just before the first meeting of the new House; the Deputy Speaker goes at once.

q.s: Who presented the Interim Union Budget 2019-20?
q.x: Piyush Goyal presented it in February 2019.

q.s: Who presented the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 as Finance Minister?
q.x: Payyavula Keshav presented it on 14 February 2026; Atchannaidu presented the agriculture budget.

q.s: By convention, the Chairman of which Parliamentary Committee is from the Opposition?
q.x: The PAC chairman is by convention from the Opposition.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the financial committees of Parliament?
q.x: The three financial committees are PAC, Estimates and Public Undertakings.

q.s: Under Article 170(3), the number of seats in State Legislative Assemblies is frozen until:
o: The Census of 2031 is finalised in 2041
q.x: The freeze lasts till the first Census after 2026, which holds up the increase under Section 26 of the AP Reorganisation Act.

q.s: The system of electing the President of India by single transferable vote is borrowed from:
q.x: The Irish Constitution; impeachment is borrowed from the USA.

q.s: The procedure for impeachment of the President of India is borrowed from the Constitution of:
q.x: Impeachment comes from the US Constitution.

q.s: The office of the Attorney General of India is provided under Article:
q.x: Article 76; the Advocate General of a State is under Article 165.

q.s: The Advocate General of a State is appointed by the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
q.x: Under Article 165 the Governor appoints the Advocate General.

q.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State (1953)?
q.x: Prakasam headed Andhra State from 1 October 1953.

q.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of the united Andhra Pradesh (1956)?
q.x: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy took office on 1 November 1956; Burgula was the first CM of Hyderabad State.

q.s: The Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law) was added to the Constitution by the:
q.x: The 52nd Amendment came into force on 1 March 1985.

q.s: Which State was the first to enact its own anti-defection law, in 1979?
q.x: Jammu and Kashmir enacted an anti-defection law in 1979.

q.s: The limit of 15% on the size of a State Council of Ministers is provided under Article:
q.x: Article 164(1A) for States and 75(1A) for the Union, both added by the 91st Amendment.

q.s: The GST Council is provided for under Article:
q.x: Article 279A (101st Amendment).

q.s: The Contingency Fund of India is provided under Article:
q.x: Article 267; Article 266 deals with the Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts.

q.s: Special Category Status was first given in 1969 on the recommendation of the 5th Finance Commission headed by:
q.x: Mahavir Tyagi headed the 5th FC; K.C. Neogy the 1st.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for granting Special Category Status?
q.x: The criterion is low per capita income, along with hilly terrain, sparse population and border location.

q.s: Disputes regarding the election of the President of India are decided by the:
q.x: Under Article 71, such disputes go to the Supreme Court.

q.s: Under Article 103, the President decides on the disqualification of an MP after obtaining the opinion of the:
q.x: The President acts according to the Election Commission's opinion; Article 192 provides the same for the Governor and MLAs.

q.s: A Joint State Public Service Commission is created by:
o: A joint order of the Governors
q.x: Under Article 315(2), Parliament creates it by law after the States' Legislatures pass resolutions, so it is a statutory body.

q.s: The Governing Council of NITI Aayog consists of the Prime Minister, all Chief Ministers and the:
q.x: The Governing Council comprises the PM, the Chief Ministers and the Lieutenant Governors.

q.s: The National Development Council was set up in the year:
q.x: The NDC was set up by an executive order on 6 August 1952.

q.s: The headquarters of the Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission is at:
q.x: The AP SHRC, constituted under the PHRA 1993, is headquartered at Kurnool.

q.s: The 2019 amendment to the Protection of Human Rights Act reduced the term of NHRC members to:
q.x: The 2019 amendment cut the term from five to three years.

q.s: Under the 2019 amendment to the PHRA, the number of deemed (ex officio) members of the NHRC was raised from four to:
q.x: Deemed members rose to seven; expert members rose to three, one of whom must be a woman.

q.s: Under the RTI Act, 2005, the normal time limit for a PIO to reply to a request is:
q.x: 30 days normally; 48 hours where life or liberty is involved; 35 days through an APIO.

q.s: Under the RTI Act, a second appeal to the Information Commission must be filed within:
q.x: The second appeal lies within 90 days of the first appellate decision.

q.s: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill, 2011 became an Act in the year:
q.x: It was enacted as the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.

q.s: The 'Single Directive' requiring prior sanction to probe senior officers was struck down in:
q.x: Vineet Narain struck it down; it was later put into law as Section 6A of the DSPE Act.

q.s: Section 6A of the DSPE Act, which required prior sanction to investigate senior officers, was struck down in:
o: Vineet Narain v. Union of India (1997)
q.x: The Constitution Bench struck down Section 6A in 2014.

q.s: Which of the following central agencies requires the general consent of a State Government to investigate in that State?
q.x: The CBI works under the DSPE Act and needs State consent; the ED and NIA do not.

q.s: Which State challenged the NIA Act, 2008 in the Supreme Court in January 2020?
q.x: Chhattisgarh filed a suit under Article 131 against the NIA Act.

q.s: Who described Indian federalism as 'cooperative federalism'?
q.x: Austin; Wheare called it quasi-federal and Morris-Jones 'bargaining federalism'.

q.s: Who described the Indian Constitution as 'quasi-federal'?
q.x: K.C. Wheare; Jennings called it a federation with a strong centralising tendency.

q.s: The M.M. Punchhi Commission (2007) was set up to examine:
q.x: The Second Commission on Centre-State Relations was headed by Justice Punchhi.

q.s: Under Article 357, laws made by Parliament for a State during President's Rule:
o: Continue until altered by the State Legislature
q.x: They remain in force after President's Rule until the State Legislature changes them.

q.s: The High-Level Committee on simultaneous elections ('One Nation, One Election') was chaired by:
q.x: Former President Ram Nath Kovind chaired it.

q.s: Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections were held together from 1951-52 till:
q.x: The cycle broke after 1967.

q.s: The National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj (NIRDPR) is located at:
q.x: NIRDPR is in Hyderabad.

q.s: Under the SVAMITVA scheme, rural inhabited land is mapped using:
o: Drone surveys by the Survey of India
q.x: SVAMITVA uses drone surveys to issue property cards (Record of Rights).

q.s: Under the three-tier Panchayati Raj model of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, the executive body was the:
q.x: The Panchayat Samiti was executive and the Zila Parishad advisory and supervisory.

q.s: Under the Balwant Rai Mehta model, the Zila Parishad was to be chaired by the:
o: Minister in charge of the district
q.x: The Collector was to be the chairman of the Zila Parishad.

q.s: The practice of 'sarpanch-pati' refers to:
o: A sarpanch nominated by the Collector
A male relative running the office of an elected woman sarpanch
A husband and wife jointly elected as sarpanch
Reservation of sarpanch posts for married women
q.x: It is an informal proxy practice with no legal basis; the elected woman remains the office-holder.

q.s: Women's voter turnout exceeded that of men for the first time in which Lok Sabha election?
q.x: In 2019 women's turnout was higher than men's for the first time.

q.s: The SVEEP programme for voter education is run by the:
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
q.x: SVEEP (Systematic Voters' Education and Electoral Participation) is the ECI's programme.

q.s: Who was the first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
q.x: Meira Kumar became Speaker in 2009.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (first woman - office) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Meira Kumar - Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Sucheta Kripalani - Governor of a State
Pratibha Bharati - Speaker of the AP Assembly
Sarojini Naidu - Governor of a State
q.x: Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister (UP, 1963); Sarojini Naidu the first woman Governor.

q.s: An Eklavya Model Residential School is to be set up in every block with more than 50% ST population and at least how many tribal persons?
q.x: EMRS norms: over 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons.

q.x: The Dongria Kondh Gram Sabhas rejected the mining under the Forest Rights Act.

o: Leases of tribal land in Scheduled Areas to private mining companies
Reservation of teacher posts for local STs
q.x: Samatha held that mining in Scheduled Areas could be done only by State undertakings or tribal cooperatives.

q.s: G.O. No. 3 (2000) of Andhra Pradesh, struck down by the Supreme Court in 2020, provided:
o: 100% reservation of teacher posts in Scheduled Areas for local STs
Ban on mining in Scheduled Areas
q.x: The Constitution Bench struck down the 100% reservation in 2020.

q.s: Appeals against orders of SEBI lie before the:
q.x: SAT also hears appeals against IRDAI and PFRDA orders.

q.s: Under the FSSAI reforms of 2026, a Central licence is required for food businesses with turnover above:
q.x: Registration up to Rs 1.5 crore, State licence Rs 1.5-50 crore, Central licence above Rs 50 crore.

q.s: According to the Global MPI 2018, how many Indians moved out of multidimensional poverty between 2005-06 and 2015-16?
q.x: The 2018 Global MPI reported 271 million people out of poverty in that decade.

q.s: As per the NSS 75th round (2017-18), which State had the lowest literacy rate (age 7+)?

q.x: The urban share rose from about 11% in 1901 to 31.1% in 2011.

q.x: A nine-judge Bench located privacy in Article 21.

q.x: The six cities were Indore, Rajkot, Chennai, Ranchi, Agartala and Lucknow.

q.s: GST was introduced in India on:
q.x: GST came into force on 1 July 2017, in 2017-18.

q.s: In India, the largest share of the workforce is still employed in the:

q.s: The new GDP series of India released in 2026 uses the base year:
q.x: The revised series has base year 2022-23.

q.x: Tertiary about 52.9%, secondary 25.8% and primary 21.4%.

q.x: Nurkse: low income - low saving - low investment - low productivity - low income.

It was set up by an Act of Parliament.

q.x: India reached 63rd place in 2019.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh has held the top rank in the Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP) since:
q.x: AP has been No. 1 since BRAP 2016.

q.s: The Finance Commission of India is constituted under Article:

q.x: Parvathipuram Manyam was carved out of Vizianagaram; YSR Kadapa continues.

q.s: Sustainable Development Goal 14 relates to:

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Rs 2,000 notes withdrawn in May 2023 is correct?
o: They were withdrawn under a new demonetisation law.
They ceased to be legal tender on withdrawal.
They continue to be legal tender.

q.s: Flexible inflation targeting was adopted by the RBI on the recommendation of the:

q.s: The residuary power of taxation under the Indian Constitution rests with:
q.x: Residuary powers, including taxation, lie with Parliament.

q.s: The Cost Inflation Index used for indexation of capital gains has the base year:

q.s: India's current account deficit peaked at about 4.8% of GDP in:

q.s: FEMA, which made foreign-exchange violations civil offences, replaced the:

q.s: India's present exchange-rate system is best described as a:

q.x: Gram is a pulse; groundnut is an oilseed and paddy a cereal.
